fixture.removed_assumption: atomic coupling between effect:E execution and durable marker M_E creation
counterexample_schedule: A0 is current, passes the commit-time authority/fence predicate, M_E is absent, and effect:E has not yet executed.
A0 crashes before durable marker M_E is created; the external/nontransactional effect remains observable while M_E remains absent.
On retry, a current claimant (A0 if still current, or A1 after a legitimate authority turnover) passes the then-current commit-time authority/fence predicate and observes M_E absent.
The retry executes effect:E again, producing a duplicate effect, and then creates durable marker M_E.
Later retries observe M_E present and are suppressed, but the duplicate has already occurred.
fixture.duplicate_effect_search: A duplicate effect is exhibited in the crash window because the first effect survives while the idempotency marker does not yet exist.
fixture.authority_check: Current-authority-only execution can remain satisfied for both attempts: each actor may be legitimately current at its own commit-time fence check. The failure is therefore distinct from stale-authority TOCTOU and is caused by the non-atomic effect/marker boundary.

observations: Restoring commit-time fencing removes the prior stale-authority defect but does not close the crash window between a nontransactional effect and durable idempotency-marker creation.

A durable marker prevents duplicates only after it exists; if effect:E survives a crash that occurs before marker persistence, a later valid current claimant can repeat the effect without violating authority fencing.

This separates two independent safety dimensions: authority correctness needs commit-time fencing, while duplicate suppression across crashes needs atomic effect/marker coupling or an equivalent recoverable protocol.
inference: Within this exact abstract model, true exactly-once useful effects cannot be inferred from durable idempotency plus commit-time fencing when the useful effect is nontransactional relative to marker persistence. A concrete accepted mechanism must either atomically commit the effect and durable idempotency state, make the effect itself intrinsically idempotent under a stable effect key, or provide a recoverable protocol whose crash states cannot repeat or lose the intended effect. This does not establish any concrete Chat-exposed transport, CAS primitive, transaction facility, lease implementation, or real multi-claimant system.
unresolved_children: A concrete allowed zero-cost quota-independent Chat-exposed primitive or protocol that couples current-authority fencing with crash-safe idempotent effect execution remains unverified.

Reservation-before-effect protocols may prevent duplicates but can lose the effect when a crash occurs after reservation and before execution; that loss-mode negative control remains untested in the current bounded slice.

A next local negative control should pre-create/reserve the durable effect marker before effect execution, retain commit-time fencing, then crash after reservation but before effect:E to test whether duplicate avoidance is traded for permanent lost-effect risk.
